content_zh: 德国驻上海总领事馆文化教育处，上海，2026

由五金机电串联起来的街巷日常是否能为我们重新理解生产活动和社群关系提供新鲜的现实切口？日用工具和手工技能如何激活技术作为组织形式的视角与感知？由布展工EXHIBITECHS策划的艺术活动“拆装手册”在上海的“五金街”开展了一场考察，试图追寻手工技能与五金产业之间的动态关联，通过技术的视角探索五金机电类生产资料的流通、应用，及其与地方社群的交互；同时借由以“拆装”为核心的手工工作坊，想象知识和经验的交换与重组。活动依托德国驻上海总领事馆文化教育处“歌德开放空间”的项目框架而举办，并得到了来自新时线媒体艺术中心（CAC）的支持。

活动的第一阶段召集公众在上海历史上的五金街区域（黄浦区北京东路附近）走访五金店、电子商场、维修点、回收站、建筑工地等流通节点，并通过购买、置换等方式收集电动工具、机械仪器、日用配件等五金机电物品，同时与收集过程中遇到的店铺老板、工具买家、维修人员、社区技工、建筑工人等个体/群体进行对话。探索内容包括：国营五金商店的转型历程，五金杂货店的街区记忆，维修站点的技艺传递，以及当代电子商业的跨国网络等等。

以家具和电器的拆装说明书，以及逆向工程中的技术解密档案为灵感，活动的第二阶段通过工作坊的形式，邀请参与者选用走访过程收集来的实体器件，通过拆装和改造，创作一批“信息装置”——即“拆装手册”。这些“手册”一方面记录和呈现所拆器物的内外结构，不同零部件的材质、功能和配合关系，以及相关的制造工艺与流通环节；另一方面，也涵盖被器物牵扯出的社群关系、具身知识与感性经验：五金店、维修铺、装修师傅、电子市场差异化的物资组织形态，一代代劳动者在实操中沉淀下来的、与技术共处的生存巧思，还有各行各业的人在工件流转里留下的指纹与目光。
同时，活动也邀请了来自复旦大学的研究者楚童分享其团队于2021-22年开展的五金街研究项目，从历史和城市的视角向参与者讲述北京东路、上海五金产业的缘起和发展，以及街区内的五金人与社会生活。
content_en: Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany in Shanghai, Shanghai, 2026

Can the neighbourhood everydayness woven together by hardware supplies offer us a fresh, grounded entry point to re-understand production and community? How might everyday tools and manual skills activate perspectives and perceptions of technology as a form of organisation? Curated by 布展工EXHIBITECHS, the event 'Teardown Manuals' puts together a social investigation into the 'hardware streets' in Shanghai, and a workshop of hands-on (dis)assembly, exploring the dynamics between technology and community within the circulation and application of hardware-related means of production, while imagining the exchange and reconfiguration of knowledge, skills, and experience. The event was organised within the framework of the 'Goethe Open Space' project of the Cultural and Educational Section of the German Consulate General in Shanghai, with support from the Chronus Art Center (CAC).

The first phase of the event invites publics to visit hardware stores, electronics markets, repair shops, recycling centers, construction sites, and other circulation nodes in Shanghai's historic 'Hardware Street' area (near Beijing East Road in Huangpu District). Participants collect electromechanical items -- such as power tools, mechanical instruments, and everyday accessories -- through purchase or exchange, while engaging in conversations with individuals and groups encountered during the collection process, including shop owners, tool buyers, repair technicians, community handymen, and construction workers. The visits and chats explore topics such as the transformation of state-owned hardware outlets, the neighborhood memories associated with general hardware stores, the transmission of technical skills at repair shops, and the transnational networks of contemporary electronics commerce.

Drawing inspiration from assembly and disassembly manuals for furniture and appliances, as well as technical decryption archives from reverse engineering, the second phase of the event takes the form of a hands-on workshop. Participants are invited to select physical components collected during their field visits and, through disassembly, reassembly, and modification, create a series of 'information installations' -- that is, 'teardown manuals'. On the one hand, these 'manuals' document and present the internal and external structures of the disassembled objects, the materials, functions, and interrelationships of their various components, as well as the relevant manufacturing processes and distribution channels; on the other hand, they also encompass the social relationships, embodied knowledge, and sensory experiences evoked by these objects: the diverse organizational forms of material resources found in hardware stores, repair shops, renovation contractors, and electronics markets; the practical ingenuity developed over generations of workers as they coexist with technology; and the fingerprints and gazes left by people from all walks of life as these objects passed through their hands.

The event also features Chu Tong, a researcher from Fudan University, to share her team's 2021–22 research project on the Hardware Street. From historical and urban perspectives, Chu discusses with participants the origins and development of East Beijing Road and Shanghai's hardware industry, as well as the lives and social interactions in the neighborhood.
